expectations.real_bar: To rise, the release needs a FY revenue outlook no worse than the street's roughly RMB11.3bn (so any cut is no deeper than the street already assumes), plus commentary that China volume and early credit indicators have bottomed and continued buybacks at a valuation below cash. A Qfin-style 'third cut, further erosion' Q4 outlook sells it.

next_guide.street_full_year: FY2026 revenue RMB11.31bn average (10.9-11.6), EPS RMB5.32 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/finv/forecast/, single source)
next_guide.company_current_guide: FY2026 total revenue RMB11.5-12.9bn, 'lower part of the range unless the operating environment substantially changes' (2026-08-27 release and call). No quarterly guide.
next_guide.basis: The street already sits below the low end. Qfin cut again on 2026-11-24, with a Q4 net income guide down 67-77% year on year and the CEO calling for 'regulatory uncertainties likely to persist' into 2027. Lexin guided a possible Q3 net loss. FINV's own call reported China volume down about 50% in July and early risk indicators up about 20%. A formal cut to about RMB11.0-11.5bn is the likely case, roughly at the street's figure.

findings.finding: Qfin, the largest US-listed peer in the same China consumer-credit facilitation channel, reported Q3 2026 on 2026-11-24 after FINV last spoke. It beat a lowered bar, with non-GAAP net income of RMB416.5m against a guide of 400-500m. It then guided Q4 net income to RMB210-310m (non-GAAP 250-350m, down 67-77% year on year), reported a 90+ day delinquency of 2.50%, day-1 delinquency of 5.8% and loan volume down 40.6% year on year, and the CEO cited 'clear erosion in risk performance', an 'industry-wide liquidity squeeze' and regulation persisting into 2027. QFIN fell 11.2% on 2026-11-25. The read-through is that FINV's Q4 and FY commentary is likely to show the same deterioration.
findings.link: Same business, regulation and funding channel. Both facilitate unsecured consumer loans for Chinese bank and trust partners under the NFRA notice effective 2025-10-01 and the 2026 debt-collection crackdown. China is about 70% of FINV's revenue (overseas was 27-30% in H1 2026). FINV's own Q2 call cited the same funding tightening and collection-capacity squeeze. Customers and lenders overlap at the industry level, but no shared-customer figure was found.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FINV fell 15.4% after Q2 2026 on the 'lower part' FY guide and the warned Q3 China contraction (2026-08-28). QFIN's Q3 2025 print slid 13% after hours, as did FINV's Q3 2025 (-13.9% on 2025-11-20).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: FINV fell 4.6% on 11-25 against QFIN's -11.2%, so the full read-through is not in FINV's price. If it were fully priced, FINV would have matched QFIN's move or its implied move would have widened. The preview implied move fell from 23.1% to 11.8%.
findings.independence: Qfin's own 2026-11-16 preview reported first-payment defaults up about 20% month on month in August and funding costs up about 25bp (https://finviz.com/news/423403/qfins-profit-floor-faces-its-first-test-as-credit-stress-and-funding-costs-bite). That is the same company, so it is not independent of this finding. FINV's own Q2 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15496818263843840) points the same way.

findings.finding: FINV's FY2026 revenue guide is RMB11.5-12.9bn, at the 'lower part'. The street's average is already below the low end at RMB11.31bn (range 10.9-11.6bn; EPS RMB5.32, down 47.6%). The H2 revenue the street implies (about 4.70bn against H1 of 6.61bn) means a formal cut to about 11.0-11.5bn would match expectations. Only a cut below about RMB10.9bn, or a Q4 profit outlook as steep as Qfin's, is new negative information.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance moved the stock at the last two prints: -15.4% on 2026-08-28 on the 'lower part' language, and +10.2% on 2026-05-26 with a reaffirmed guide plus a new $150m buyback.
findings.why_not_priced: The street's figure is already below the guide, so a cut to that level is priced. What is not priced is how deep the cut goes and what the Q4 profit trajectory looks like after Qfin's 2026-11-24 data point. If a deep cut were priced, the stock would have fallen as far as QFIN on 11-25.
findings.independence: Company guide: https://www.financialcontent.com/article/gnwcq-2026-8-27-finvolution-group-reports-second-quarter-2026-unaudited-financial-results . The Lexin Q3 2026 warning of a possible net loss (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/LexinFintech+Reports+Second+Quarter+2026+Unaudited+Financial+Results+and+Updates+Dividend+Policy) is an independent peer pointing the same way.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call (2026-08-27) FINV said China volume was 'down around 50% in July', early risk indicators were 'up around 20% versus the second quarter', funding cost rose 30bp to 3.7% with 'further upward pressure' expected, and the collection crackdown hurt recovery efficiency. Q3 provisions and margin should therefore be weaker than Q2, which had net profit of RMB426.8m. The company has already told the market this, so the item sits inside guidance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The reported quarter has mattered less than the guide: Q2 2026 net profit down 43% was absorbed into a guide-driven -15.4%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced, because it is the company's own public warning. What is left is the size of the credit-cost step-up, which has no quarterly consensus to compare against. If the market had underestimated it, the stock would not have held a 4.6% loss against QFIN's 11%.
findings.independence: Qfin reported day-1 delinquency of 5.8% and 90+ day delinquency of 2.50% in Q3 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001741530/000110465926131684/tm2630464d1_ex99-1.htm). That source is shared with the first finding.

findings.finding: FINV trades below its cash. Cash plus short-term investments were RMB6.42bn (US$946m) at 2026-06-30, and management cited RMB7.5bn of cash plus about RMB5bn of highly liquid assets on the call. The market cap is about US$556m (roughly 238m ADS, inferred from 5.0m short shares being 2.1% of shares outstanding, × $2.335). The company has a $150m buyback authorised from 2026-05-30 to 2028-05-29 and bought $66.8m in H1. The Q3 release normally discloses the buyback amount, and any acceleration or new return at this valuation is a long-side catalyst.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 2026 print, announced with the new $150m buyback, rose 10.2% (2026-05-26; Simply Wall St notes about +15% after the news).
findings.why_not_priced: The valuation is visible, but the market has looked through it through a 62% drawdown. The new information is the Q3 repurchase pace, which is not public until the release. If an acceleration were priced, the stock would not be at a fresh 52-week low.
findings.independence: Buyback programme: https://finviz.com/news/356760/finvolution-group-announces-new-share-repurchase-program-of-up-to-us150-million . The share count is my inference from https://equibles.com/stocks/finv/shortinterest , so it is a proxy.

findings.finding: The setup into the print is washed out. The stock is down 10.5% over 5 days and 17.5% over 20 days to a 52-week low, 62% below its high and about 58% below the mean target of $5.61. The implied move has compressed to about 11.8% from 23.1% before the last print. The bar the price holds is low, which gives the reaction some asymmetry if the guide is only 'at street'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A depressed setup has not protected this name: Q3 2025 (-13.9%) and Q2 2026 (-15.4%) both fell further.
findings.why_not_priced: This item describes the price, so it is priced by definition. What it adds is how the next session reacts, and that asymmetry is the bet. Weekly peer moves of -6% to -15% show the drawdown is sector-wide, not FINV-specific.
findings.independence: Baseline tape (run-up fields) and https://www.investing.com/equities/ppdai-consensus-estimates for targets.

findings.finding: Indonesia's OJK P2P lending data for September 2026 shows the industry's 90+ day default rate (TWP90) at 5.36%, up from 4.73% in August and above OJK's 5% threshold, with outstanding-loan growth slowing to 17.0% year on year from 22.1%. FINV's overseas business (Indonesia via AdaKami, plus the Philippines) is 27-30% of revenue and was its growth offset. This points to higher overseas credit costs in Q3 and Q4.
findings.link: AdaKami is FINV's OJK-licensed Indonesian P2P platform. Overseas revenue was RMB930m in Q2 (27% of the total). No AdaKami-specific figure was found.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The overseas segment has been the positive offset in recent prints (Q2 overseas operating profit more than doubled); no reaction to an overseas miss is on record.
findings.why_not_priced: This is local-language industry data that the US sell-side previews do not cite. If it were priced, the overseas 'growth offset' narrative would already be discounted, but the targets still lean on it.
findings.independence: https://keuangan.kontan.co.id/news/pembiayaan-fintech-lending-tumbuh-1702-per-september-2026-twp90-tembus-536 (different outlet, same OJK data). This is a macro proxy, not company data.

findings.finding: Chinese banks are cutting their online-platform partnerships. Jilin Yillion Bank went from 56 customer-acquisition partners in November 2024 to 10 in July 2026. Online-marketing measures for financial products took effect on 30 September, and regulators told e-commerce apps on 21 September to stop selling loans. Funding and traffic stay tight into Q4. China Daily also expects leading platforms to gain share as smaller ones exit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Regulatory tightening drove the 2026 de-rating across the group; FINV's guide-driven -15.4% in August cited funding tightening.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced in the sector drawdown. What remains is whether the funding squeeze FINV said would last 'one or two quarters' extends into Q4.
findings.independence: Sixth Tone on e-commerce lending (https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019049/China Tells E-Commerce Apps to Stop Selling Loans). Caixin 2026-09-10 calls FINV 'relatively resilient' (https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-09-10/chinas-online-lenders-see-profits-plunge-as-new-rules-bite-102483449.html).

findings.finding: FINV is the relative survivor of its group. In H1 2026 revenue fell about 6% and profit about 43%, against Qfin's revenue -25%, Jiayin's first interim loss (Q2 volume RMB9.5bn), X Financial's Q2 volume -70% and Vcredit's -84%. Lexin guided a possible Q3 net loss. Peers trade at $0.25 (YRD, with an NYSE price notice) to $1.17 (JFIN). If competitors exit, leading platforms can take share and acquisition costs fall.
findings.link: Same China loan-facilitation channel and regulation. The share-gain mechanism is that banks consolidate onto fewer platforms (China Daily 2026-10-22). No FINV-specific share figure was found.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No record of FINV being rewarded for relative resilience; it has traded with the group.
findings.why_not_priced: FINV still fell with the group on 11-25 (-4.6%) and over the week (-9.4%). If the market priced its relative position, it would have decoupled from Lexin and Qfin.
findings.independence: Qfin's own Q3 2026 release mentions competitor exits cutting industry acquisition spend (https://finviz.com/news/423403/qfins-profit-floor-faces-its-first-test-as-credit-stress-and-funding-costs-bite). YRD price notice: https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=YRD

findings.finding: Short interest rose 10.7% in the two weeks to 2026-11-13 (4.48m to 4.96m shares) and days to cover went from 4.45 to 7.60. About 3.8% of float is short, so new shorts are building into the print but the position is not crowded.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No squeeze history on record; float short has stayed in low single digits.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is published with a lag. The building short is informational at most; at 3.8% of float it is too small to drive a squeeze.

findings.finding: Analyst targets have not moved since 2026-08-28 (Citi Hold $4.10, Jefferies Buy $4.70; mean $5.61, all at least 75% above spot), and the targets for a 'Strong Buy' consensus look stale. Post-print target cuts toward spot are likely and would land in the session.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Citi's downgrade landed on the -15.4% session in August.
findings.why_not_priced: Stale targets are a known condition. The fact is small and mostly priced.

baseline_tension: The skew is null and the run-up is deeply negative, so the negative peer read-through runs with the price trend into a washed-out setup. That is why p_up sits at 44 rather than lower, and the cash-backed buyback item offsets part of it.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar unsourced, finding inside what the company already guided): Q2-call warnings of July volume -50% and risk indicators +20% cut from -1.0 to -0.5, filed as reported_quarter.
Rule 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the below-cash buyback item cut from +2.0 to +1.5, because the market has looked through the valuation through a 62% drawdown.
Rule 5 (proxy smaller): Indonesia OJK data cut from -0.5 to -0.4 and the China Daily regulatory item from -0.5 to -0.4.

Reaction-history lesson for foreign private issuers: the base rate was rebuilt from confirmed prints (15.4/10.2/4.9/13.9 plus Unusual Whales' 7.0% average over 12), so abs_move stays 12. p_up was left at 44, so the scaled number is unchanged.
